bill.title: Election Law Changes.

posted_text:
📝 NC HB 958 — NC Changes Rules on Voter Ballots & Early Voting

North Carolina is updating its election rules.

The state board can’t use its role to push voters toward a specific political party.

If a voter’s registration challenge is upheld, their registration and any associated ballot will be canceled or corrected.

For early voting, counties must offer at least one site for every 30,000 registered voters, prioritizing geographic diversity.

Counties can propose early voting plans, but the State Board can step in if a plan disproportionately favors a party or group.

The state will conduct a sample hand-to-eye count of paper ballots in every county, and the State Board Auditor will select the sample precincts for each election.

Finally, absentee ballots will only be counted if two individuals witness their casting, and cure documentation must be received by the county board no later than 5:00 P.M.

on the third business day after the election.

Aug. 31, 2026: Placed On Cal For 09/02/2026.

🔗 Read the full bill: https://www.ncleg.gov/BillLookUp/2025/HB958
